external_primary_source_observations.observed: Current llama.cpp CLI documents --control-vector-scaled and --control-vector-layer-range, providing signed-scale and layer-range intervention controls.
Current llama.cpp includes a cvector-generator and an example that applies a generated control vector to a selected layer range.
Current llama.cpp has an activation-level cvec application implementation with model embedding-dimension checks and explicit layer-range state.

Groq currently documents logit_bias as not supported by its models; this hosted surface therefore does not provide even token-logit vector bias through that field, much less hidden-state cvec control.

OpenRouter documents logit_bias as token-logit bias. This is a token-output distribution control surface, not evidence of model-internal layer activation injection and therefore does not satisfy the Trigger-1 latent/cvec success law by itself.
